headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test is generally not recommended when fewer than 10 studies are available.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 2 studies yielded an effect size of 1.19 (95% CI: 0.47–3.01), indicating no statistically significant association between phosphorus and bladder cancer. Although the point estimate suggests a potential positive relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by substantial heterogeneity (I² = 64.00%), reflecting considerable variability across studies.
